abstract_sentences.text: Assessing Large Language Models’ (LLMs) underlying value differences enables comprehensive comparison of their misalignment, cultural adaptability, and biases.

evidence.anchor: enables comprehensive comparison of their misalignment

abstract_sentences.text: Nevertheless, current value measurement methods face the informativeness challenge: with often outdated, contaminated, or generic test questions, they can only capture the orientations on common safety values, e.g., HHH, shared among different LLMs, leading to indistinguishable and uninformative results.
abstract_sentences.comparison: Current value measurement methods versus a distinguishable measurement ideal.

evidence.anchor: current value measurement methods face the informativeness challenge

abstract_sentences.text: To address this problem, we introduce AdAEM, a novel, self-extensible evaluation algorithm for revealing LLMs’ inclinations.
abstract_sentences.transition: To address moves from gap to proposal.

abstract_sentences.text: Distinct from static benchmarks, AdAEM automatically and adaptively generates and extends its test questions.
abstract_sentences.transition: Distinct from makes the nearest contrast explicit.

abstract_sentences.text: This is achieved by probing the internal value boundaries of a diverse set of LLMs developed across cultures and time periods in an in-context optimization manner.
abstract_sentences.comparison: LLMs across cultures and time periods.

abstract_sentences.text: Such a process theoretically maximizes an information-theoretic objective to extract diverse controversial topics that can provide more distinguishable and informative insights about models’ value differences.
abstract_sentences.transition: Such a process formalizes the mechanism.

abstract_sentences.text: In this way, AdAEM is able to co-evolve with the development of LLMs, consistently tracking their value dynamics.
abstract_sentences.transition: In this way draws the capability consequence.

abstract_sentences.text: We use AdAEM to generate novel questions and conduct an extensive analysis, demonstrating our method’s validity and effectiveness, laying the groundwork for better interdisciplinary research on LLMs’ values and alignment.
abstract_sentences.comparison: No named baseline or numeric result.
abstract_sentences.transition: Moves from capability to evidence and impact.

evidence.anchor: demonstrating our method’s validity and effectiveness

abstract_sentences.text: Codes and the generated evaluation questions are released at https://github.com/ValueCompass/AdAEM.

evidence.anchor: Codes and the generated evaluation questions are released

abstract_analysis.reported_results: Only a qualitative validity/effectiveness statement; no number, baseline name, or uncertainty.

evidence.anchor: existing value benchmarks face the informativeness challenge

introduction_moves.prior_open_question: How should LLM social risks be diagnosed holistically?
introduction_moves.current_answer: Value theory is a holistic proxy, but current questions yield saturated shared safety values.
introduction_moves.next_hook: A dynamic method must elicit distinguishable values.

introduction_moves.prior_open_question: How can questions expose latent value differences?
introduction_moves.current_answer: Probe cross-cultural and cross-temporal model boundaries with in-context information optimization.
introduction_moves.next_hook: The paper must establish novelty, quality, and an artifact.

introduction_moves.current_answer: A dynamic method, comparative evidence on question quality/value elicitation, and a generated dataset.
introduction_moves.next_hook: Position the work relative to value and dynamic evaluation literatures.

introduction_analysis.chain: context → risk diagnosis → measurement-theory criterion → informativeness failure → controversial boundary probing → dynamic optimization → three contributions
introduction_analysis.analysis: The three contributions repeat the abstract method/effectiveness arc but add auditable objects. The firstness claim depends on literature coverage; question quality and value-difference claims are testable.

related_work_moves.comparison_dimension: Reasoning, QA, math, and safety applications.

related_work_analysis.nearest_neighbor_gap: No component-level comparison against an active dynamic value-question generator; the three experimental baselines are static.

assumptions: LLM values are reflected in generated opinions.
Question value should be disentangled from response value.
Proxy classifiers/coherence scores approximate inaccessible probabilities for black-box LLMs.

theory_analysis.external_result: Agakov (2005), Proposition 2.1, cited for IM lower-bound monotonicity.
theory_analysis.assumption_to_conclusion: Ideal distributions and exact expectations lead to an EM-like lower-bound optimization; practical black-box scoring substitutes classifiers, Jaccard, and BERTScore.
theory_analysis.empirical_correspondence: Figures 7 and 18 track proxy score; Appendix I compares approximate and exact implementations at profile level.
theory_analysis.unclosed_scope: No end-to-end convergence or validity guarantee covers Monte Carlo sampling, LLM-based question rewriting, UCB exploration, and the practical proxy together.

experimental_design.name: Predeclared research questions
experimental_design.description: No numbered RQs or hypotheses; §4 previews construction, validity/quality, and extensibility analyses.

experimental_design.name: Value ontology
experimental_design.description: Main experiments instantiate Schwartz ten-value theory; Appendix J instantiates five-dimensional Moral Foundation Theory.

experimental_design.name: Seed datasets
experimental_design.description: Touché23-ValueEval and ValueBench are expanded, filtered, clustered, categorized, sampled, and transformed into 1,535 generic topics.

experimental_design.name: Main benchmark configuration
experimental_design.description: B=1500, N2=3, P1 has four faster models, P2 has nine cross-cultural/cross-temporal models; output is 12,310 questions.

experimental_design.name: Geographic coverage
experimental_design.description: The generated dataset covers 106 nation-states.

experimental_design.name: Evaluatee models
experimental_design.description: Figure 9 reports 16 popular LLMs; Table 3 lists 19 models used across the paper.

experimental_design.name: Baselines
experimental_design.description: SVS, ValueBench, and ValueDCG; Appendix C.5 describes them as fixed/static approaches.

experimental_design.name: Question-quality metrics
experimental_design.description: Question count, average length, Self-BLEU, Dist-2, average semantic similarity, and t-SNE visualization.

evidence.anchor: semantic diversity and richer topic details

experimental_design.name: Human evaluation
experimental_design.description: 300 question pairs, five annotators, three-point Likert ratings for Rationality, Controversy, and Value Elicitation.

experimental_design.name: Construct-validity intervention
experimental_design.description: o3-mini and GPT-5 receive target-value system prompts; target, same-group, and opposite-group outcomes are compared.

experimental_design.name: Value classifier
experimental_design.description: GPT-4o-Mini is used during generation and GPT-4o during evaluation; 1,920 target-domain and 14k other-domain test cases audit the classifier.

experimental_design.name: Classifier metric labels
experimental_design.description: Table 4 reports slash-separated pairs such as 92.92/93.08 without naming the two metrics.

experimental_design.name: Sampling and prompts
experimental_design.description: Each model produces one response with three ordered points; each point is capped at 250 words. top_p=0.95 and temperature=1.0.

experimental_design.name: Random seeds
experimental_design.description: Five random partitions and random subsamples are used, but a reproducible random seed is not reported.

evidence.anchor: randomly divided the dataset into 5 distinct partitions

experimental_design.name: Compute hardware
experimental_design.description: API calls dominate cost; retrieval and deduplication use one NVIDIA A100 80GB GPU.

experimental_design.name: API budget and wall-clock
experimental_design.description: The paper reports B and model sets but not API tokens, monetary cost, or elapsed time.

evidence.anchor: main cost of our methods are request different LLM API

experimental_design.name: Hyperparameters
experimental_design.description: Table 6 reports ε=0.85, τ=0.5, Nshot=5, N2=3, and tree depth 3; most are defaults rather than exhaustively searched.

experimental_design.name: Contamination control
experimental_design.description: The K examinee LLMs are excluded from optimization; P1/P2 generate and score questions, with deduplication and proposed periodic regeneration.

evidence.anchor: cannot involve the real K LLMs

experimental_design.name: Longitudinal online deployment
experimental_design.description: An online AlpacaEval/ChatArena-like system is proposed as an ideal future deployment, not evaluated longitudinally.

experimental_design.name: Failure/stopping rule
experimental_design.description: Algorithm 2 stops local refinement when score gain does not exceed τ and filters near-duplicates using ε; no measurement-level failure threshold is predeclared.

experimental_design.name: Code and generated questions
experimental_design.description: The abstract links a repository; the reproducibility statement commits to releasing required data and code.

claim_closure.claim: AdAEM is a dynamic, self-extensible value-evaluation method.
claim_closure.method_response: Eq. (1)–(3), Algorithms 1–2, and the P1/P2/MAB workflow implement adaptive generation.
claim_closure.evidence_response: Regional, temporal, budget, and regeneration analyses show technical extensibility; no live longitudinal platform is evaluated.
claim_closure.conclusion_response: §6 repeats dynamic/self-extensible; Appendix C.7 labels the online platform an ideal future system.

claim_closure.claim: AdAEM generates diverse, specific, and value-evoking questions.
claim_closure.method_response: The proxy score combines value/opinion diversity, conformity, and disentanglement; MAB broadens topics.
claim_closure.evidence_response: Question metrics, human ratings, semantic maps, regional/time coverage, and failure cases directly test the generated questions.
claim_closure.conclusion_response: Conclusion claims superiority; Appendix B/C/E provide construction and detail.

claim_closure.claim: AdAEM better reveals LLM value differences.
claim_closure.method_response: Distinguishability is optimized explicitly and outputs are aggregated with relative TrueSkill.
claim_closure.evidence_response: Figure 8 and Table 15 show greater model separation, but separation is also the item-selection target and lacks independent value ground truth.

claim_closure.claim: AdAEM is a valid and reliable value measurement.
claim_closure.method_response: Opinion extraction, classifier audit, disentanglement, and relative aggregation define the measure.
claim_closure.evidence_response: Priming supports construct sensitivity/discrimination; folds support internal consistency; external criterion validity is absent.
claim_closure.conclusion_response: Conclusion says comprehensive analysis demonstrates superiority; detailed validity/reliability stays in Appendix C/K.

evidence.anchor: accurately captures the LLM’s value orientations

claim_closure.claim: AdAEM can co-evolve and continuously track value dynamics.
claim_closure.method_response: New models can be added to P and questions periodically regenerated.
claim_closure.evidence_response: Cutoff-matched snapshots support content extension, but no repeated real-time evaluation measures actual temporal value drift.
claim_closure.conclusion_response: Conclusion calls the framework dynamic; Appendix C.7 frames online deployment as a goal.

claim_closure.claim: The framework generalizes across value systems.
claim_closure.method_response: The formalization uses arbitrary dimension d and a configurable value analyzer.
claim_closure.evidence_response: Main Schwartz results plus one MFT instantiation and priming test support transfer to a second ontology.
claim_closure.conclusion_response: Conclusion says multiple value systems; Appendix J carries the evidence.

claim_closure.claim: The optimization has theoretical convergence support.
claim_closure.method_response: Appendix D maps the ideal objective to EM-like alternating optimization.
claim_closure.evidence_response: Figure 18 shows proxy-score stabilization; Appendix I audits approximation agreement.
claim_closure.conclusion_response: No conclusion claim; the guarantee is localized to Appendix E.6 and an external proposition.

limitations.name: Value-theory coverage
limitations.description: Schwartz theory is not exhaustive and no human-value framework has universal recognition.

limitations.name: Seed-data and LLM processing
limitations.description: Seeds come from two datasets and use LLM filtering/topic annotation, imposing assumptions and simplifications.

limitations.name: Model budget
limitations.description: Only representative open- and closed-source models are selected due to budget constraints.

limitations.name: Language/cultural scope
limitations.description: The main work focuses on value questions in English-speaking contexts.

limitations.name: Potential malicious use
limitations.description: Controversial-topic exploration can be misused or cause discomfort; the ethics section describes Llama-Guard filtering.

limitations.name: Ontological status of LLM values
limitations.description: Whether an LLM actually has values is declared unanswerable; value is operationalized as a behavioral latent variable.

limitations.name: Single-response sampling
limitations.description: Cost constraints limit each question to one response with three points; a preliminary 800-question consistency check supports the simplification.

limitations.name: Black-box probability approximation
limitations.description: Classifiers, Jaccard, and BERTScore substitute inaccessible probabilities; exact verification uses small open models and 100 seeds.

limitations.name: Main-body self-containment
limitations.description: Page limits move derivations, implementation, and ablations to the appendix, and the authors acknowledge reduced readability.

limitations.name: External criterion validity
limitations.description: Priming and consistency test sensitivity/reliability, but no independent ground-truth LLM value profile is supplied.

evidence.anchor: regard value as a latent variable

limitations.name: Longitudinal tracking
limitations.description: Cross-cutoff snapshots are shown, but no deployed repeated-time tracking experiment is conducted.

final_judgment.single_storyline: Static/generic value questions yield saturated shared-safety answers; AdAEM adaptively searches controversial cross-model boundaries to maximize information and then ranks model value expressions relatively.
final_judgment.main_body_keeps: The gap, qualitative motivating contrast, formal objective, E/M-like mechanism, MAB overview, TrueSkill metric, main construction configuration, core validity/reliability summaries, extensibility analyses, and the 16×10 result matrix.
final_judgment.appendix_moves: The value ontology, seed/prompt pipeline, executable proxy, complete pseudocode, classifier audit, hyperparameters, statistical details, proofs, failures, approximation audit, second ontology, and robustness analyses.
final_judgment.best_pattern: Figure 1 concrete contrast → Eq. (1) two-part objective → Figure 4 intervention check → Figure 9 decision matrix forms the strongest problem–mechanism–validation–output chain.
final_judgment.largest_gap: The generator optimizes model separation and the headline evaluation treats larger separation as evidence of truer value measurement; sensitivity and reliability are established more strongly than independent criterion validity.
final_judgment.transfer_rule: When a dynamic benchmark directly optimizes its headline metric, place the exact executable proxy in the main text and validate the construct with an intervention or external/held-out criterion independent of that proxy.
final_judgment.transfer_boundary: This rule targets adaptive item generation that reuses evaluated or neighboring model/judge signals; fixed benchmarks with independent ground truth face a smaller selection-induced-separation risk.
